object_description: cross-shaped structure with wings arranged around a central core
design_condition: the cross-shaped positioning turns only short facades towards the low-density neighbourhood, but the wide wings come critically close to the property boundaries and leave small, peripheral open spaces

positive: The positioning seeks a restrained scale by showing only short facades towards the neighbourhood
The vegetative framework of hornbeams and accent trees appears calm and natural in the context
The basic concept of wing-like classroom organisation around a public multifunctional zone is convincing
The staircase from the entrance hall also serves as an auditorium
The formulated expression with light concrete, elm wood and carefully treated metals is atmospheric
negative: The volume comes critically close to the property boundaries, so the claim of restraint is not fulfilled
The placement results in a series of small-scale and peripheral open spaces
Flat parking lots extend far into the interior of the complex, losing valuable space and hindering access
The site concept is not convincing due to its confusing, small-scale structure
The three-wing form of the first stage is not convincing; the large form only comes together in full extension
Floor plans are designed for 27 classes, forcing programmatic compromises in the 18-class stage
Addressing of the main entrance is uninviting and peripheral
The cascading open hall was sacrificed for a small-scale, diffuse central zone separated by floor ceilings
The project barely meets the requirements for fire protection, sustainability and economy
Greatly increased building and excavation volume lead to relatively high costs
Numerous uses under terrain with hardly any natural lighting have a negative impact on sustainability
The materialisation appears forced and is more reminiscent of noble residential buildings
